title: Israel seeks swift air campaign against Iran as Trump weighs options
author: Ben Caspit
text:
Analysis

Israel seeks swift air campaign against Iran as Trump weighs options

Israeli intelligence points to Iranian efforts to develop chemical and biological weapons, but sources say Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s push for a strike against the Tehran regime is driven by his own political timetable.

Ben Caspit

USAF military personnel work beneath a US Air Force B-1 Lancer bomber jet at RAF Fairford in southwest England on March 14, 2026. — Henry NICHOLLS / AFP via Getty Images

TEL AVIV — Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for an immediate, short and hard-hitting strike against Iran as concerns mount in Israel over Tehran’s intentions to develop chemical and biological weapons and fortify the Pickaxe Mountain site, Western diplomatic sources told Al-Monitor.While these concerns are rooted in intelligence assessments of the regime’s intentions, political calculations in both the United States and Israel are significant factors in any decision by the two countries to attack Iran, the sources acknowledged.Biological or chemical weapons?A Nov. 16 CNN report citing US officials said Iran was developing contingency plans for a chemical weapons or “dirty bomb” attack targeting senior officials in Washington. A Tuesday New York Times report said Israeli intelligence had warned US and Gulf counterparts that Iran’s chemical weapons program posed a more immediate threat than its nuclear ambitions, though both expressed skepticism.
